[[EuroLeague]] | team = Real Madrid | number = 8 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1998|8|18}} | birth_place = [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]], U.S. | high_school = [[Westlake High School (Georgia)|Westlake]] (Atlanta, Georgia) | college = [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] (2017–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 16 | draft_team = [[Orlando Magic]] | career_start = 2020 | years1 = {{nbay|2020|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team1 = [[Orlando Magic]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Osceola Magic|Lakeland Magic]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Westchester Knicks]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years5 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team5 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years6 = 2025–present | team6 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League Third Team]] ([[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]]) * [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]] (2017) }} '''Chukwuma Julian''' "'''Chuma'''" '''Okeke''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|tʃ|uː|m|ə|_|oʊ|ˈ|k|eɪ|k|eɪ}} {{respell|CHOO|mə|_|oh|KAY|kay}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born August 18, 1998) is an American–Nigerian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Okeke played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] before being drafted 16th overall in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]]. ==High school career== Okeke attended [[Westlake High School (Georgia)|Westlake High School]] in [[Atlanta]]. As a junior, he won the Georgia Class 6A state championship, scoring 13 points in a 68–58 win over [[Pebblebrook High School]].{{cite web|first=David|last=Purdum|title=Class AAAAAA boys: Westlake 68, Pebblebrook 58|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/class-aaaaaa-boys-westlake-pebblebrook/qZeB4jm7XtYD2EJUCSAIrN/|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=May 16, 2019}} Okeke was named [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]] after his senior season, after he averaged 24.4 points, 15 rebounds and 2.4 steals per game.{{cite web|first=Wesley|last=Sinor|title=Auburn signee Chuma Okeke is Georgia's Mr. Basketball|url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2017/03/auburn_signee_chuma_okeke_is_g.html|website=AL.com|date=March 24, 2017|access-date=May 16, 2019}} He was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was ranked among the top 50 players in his class by some scouting services.{{cite web|title=Chuma Okeke|url=https://auburntigers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3835|work=Auburn University Athletics|access-date=May 16, 2019}} ==College career== Okeke played for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]].{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Ostendorf|title=Getting to know Chuma Okeke|url=https://auburntigers.com/news/2018/2/7/Getting_to_know_Chuma_Okeke.aspx|work=Auburn University Athletics|date=February 7, 2018|access-date=May 16, 2019}} In his freshman season, Okeke averaged 7.5 points and 5.8 rebounds per game. He grabbed 197 rebounds in the season, the most by an Auburn freshman since [[Jeff Moore (basketball)|Jeff Moore]] in [[1984–85 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|1984–85]]. As a sophomore, Okeke averaged 12 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.2 blocks per game while starting in all 38 games.{{cite web|title=Chuma Okeke Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Chuma-Okeke/Summary/88842|website=RealGM.com|access-date=May 16, 2019}} On March 29, 2019, in a Sweet 16 win over top-seeded [[2018–19 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] at the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]], he [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|tore]] his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and was injured for the rest of the tournament. Despite his absence, Auburn advanced to its first Final Four appearance in program history.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Teicher|title=How Auburn survived without (and because of) Chuma Okeke |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26410108|work=[[ESPN]]|date=March 31, 2019|access-date=May 16, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2020–2024)=== On June 20, 2019, Okeke was selected with the 16th overall pick by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]]. Okeke was considered to be a lottery pick in the draft, but after suffering an [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]], he fell to the 16th selection by the Magic, and was referred to by ESPN analyst Mike Schmitz as the "steal of the draft."{{cite news|first=Philip|last=Rossman-Reich|title=While Orlando Magic fans complained, experts loved Chuma Okeke|url=https://orlandomagicdaily.com/2019/06/22/orlando-magic-fans-complained-experts-loved-chuma-okeke/|work=Orlando Magic Daily|date=June 22, 2019|access-date=November 14, 2023}} During his rehab, Okeke signed a one-year [[G League]] contract with the Magic's affiliate in [[Osceola Magic|Lakeland]] with the intent of starting his rookie-scale contract in 2020. At the time, the Magic faced a salary cap crunch that prevented them from adding Okeke's rookie salary to their books.{{cite web|first1=Shams|last1=Charania|author-link=Shams Charania|first2=Josh|last2=Robbins|name-list-style=and|title=Magic first-round pick Chuma Okeke will sign his NBA rookie scale contract during the 2020 offseason|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1235110/2019/09/23/orlando-magic-chuma-okeke-0923/|website=TheAthletic.com|date=September 24, 2019|access-date=October 29, 2019}} He reported to Lakeland's training camp as a draft rights player on October 28, 2019.{{cite web|title=2019 NBA G League Training Camp Rosters|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/2019-nba-g-league-training-camp-rosters/|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 29, 2019}} However, Okeke never played a game with Lakeland. On November 16, 2020, the [[Orlando Magic]] signed Okeke.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Savage|title=Orlando Magic Sign Rookie Chuma Okeke|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-rookie-chuma-okeke-20201116|website=NBA.com|date=November 16, 2020|access-date=November 16, 2020}} In a preseason game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Okeke recorded 9 points with 2 three-pointers. On March 26, 2021, he scored a career-high 22 points on 60 percent shooting from the field in a 105–112 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. Okeke averaged over 12 points after the trade deadline before suffering a season-ending minor ankle injury against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. On February 25, 2022, he scored a career-high 26 points in a 119–111 win over the [[Houston Rockets]], surpassing his previous career-high mark set during the [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 season]]. ===Westchester Knicks / Philadelphia 76ers (2024–2025)=== On August 1, 2024, Okeke signed with the [[New York Knicks]],{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Sign Chuma Okeke to an Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-chuma-okeke-to-an-exhibit-10-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2024|access-date=August 4, 2024}} but was waived on September 28.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Marcus Morris Sr. and Chuma Okeke|number=1840138850791796761|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=September 28, 2024|access-date=September 28, 2024}} On October 2, he re-signed with the Knicks,{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Sign Chuma Okeke to Exhibit 10 Contract|number=1841600472370839992|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 3, 2024}} but was waived again on October 19.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Chuma Okeke, Landry Shamet and T.J. Warren.|number=1847742422064734246|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 22, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2024-25 NBA G League Training Camp Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2024-25-nba-g-league-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 1, 2024}} On February 6, 2025, Okeke signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]],{{Cite web |last=Carlin |first=Ky |title=Report: Sixers to sign Chuma Okeke to 10-day deal out of the G League |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/sixers/2025/02/06/report-sixers-to-sign-chuma-okeke-to-10-day-deal-out-of-the-g-league/78298231007/ |access-date=2025-02-06 |website=Sixers Wire |language=en-US}} and on February 18, he returned to Westchester.{{Cite web |date=2025-02-18 |title=G League Knicks Welcome Back Chuma Okeke |url=https://www.si.com/nba/knicks/news/g-league-new-york-knicks-welcome-back-chuma-okeke |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=New York Knicks On SI |language=en-US}} On March 15, Okeke signed a second 10-day contract with the 76ers.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-15 |title=Report: Sixers bringing back Chuma Okeke on 10-day contract |url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/sixers-news-analysis-chuma-okeke-stats-highlights-bio-nba-hardship-exception-10-day-contracts/ |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=PhillyVoice |language=english}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2025)=== On April 3, 2025, Okeke signed a deal with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web | last1=Ulrich | first1=Nate | title=Cleveland Cavs and former 1st round pick Chuma Okeke agree to deal | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2025-04-04 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/cleveland-cavs-former-1st-round-013226387.html | access-date=2025-12-06}} He made two appearances for Cleveland, averaging 2.5 points, two rebounds, and one assist. ===Real Madrid (2025–present)=== On July 18, 2025, Okeke signed with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Chuma Okeke heads to Europe as Real Madrid secures ex-NBA
